title: Moser’s union-free subfamily conjecture
statement:

references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/01](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/4791), page 7. Canonicalized from 3 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Growth of maximum $a$-union-free subfamilies
statement:
Let $a\ge 2$ be an integer. A family of sets is called $a$-union-free if it contains no $a+1$ distinct sets $X_1,\ldots,X_a,X_{a+1}$ such that $X_1\cup\cdots\cup X_a=X_{a+1}$. Let $g(m,a)$ be the minimum, over all families of $m$ sets, of the size of the largest $a$-union-free subfamily. Conjecture 3 asserts that
\[
\lim_{a\to\infty}\,\liminf_{m\to\infty}\frac{g(m,a)}{\sqrt m}=\infty.
\]
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/01](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/4791), page 8. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Asymptotics of the clause-intersection satisfiability threshold
statement:

$$l(k)=\left(\frac{1}{e}+O\!\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{k}}\right)\right)2^k.$$

title: Equality between inversion-arrangement regions and Bruhat intervals
statement:
For a finite reflection group $W$ and $w\in W$, characterize the elements $w$ for which
$$
\#\operatorname{re}(w)=\#[e,w],
$$
where $\operatorname{re}(w)$ is the set of regions of the inversion arrangement $\mathcal A_w$ and $[e,w]$ is the Bruhat-order interval from the identity $e$ to $w$. The report states that equality holds if and only if, for every $u\le w$, at least one shortest path from $u$ to $w$ in the Cayley graph of $W$ generated by reflections visits vertices in order of increasing Coxeter length.
